# gitmoap_group_package (Data Source)

A package's detail with its versions. Returns the package with every published version: its size, whether it is yanked, and who published it when. The name is matched the way its registry matches names, so a PyPI name is normalized and a Cargo name is read in lower case. Anyone who can see the group may call it.

The token needs `package:read`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `format` (String) Registry format (npm/cargo/pypi)
- `group_id` (String) Owning group id
- `package_name` (String) Package name

### Read-Only

- `latest_version` (String) The newest version, when there is one.
- `name` (String) The package's name, as it was published.
- `total_bytes` (Number) The size of every file of every version, in bytes.
- `updated_at` (String)
- `version_count` (Number)
- `versions` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--versions))

<a id="nestedatt--versions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `versions`

Read-Only:

- `published_at` (String)
- `published_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--versions--published_by))
- `size_bytes` (Number) The size of the version's files, in bytes.
- `version` (String)
- `yanked` (Boolean) Whether the version has been yanked, as a Cargo crate version can be. Always `false` for npm
and PyPI.

<a id="nestedatt--versions--published_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `versions.published_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
